claims.reasoning: Passage [4] states this condition for a checkpoint to run to completion and reset the WAL.

citations.quote: A checkpoint is only able to run to completion, and reset the WAL file, if there are no other database connections using the WAL file.

claims.claim_text: A database with many concurrent overlapping readers and at least one always-active reader will never let a checkpoint finish, causing unbounded WAL growth.
claims.reasoning: Passage [5] states this exact scenario and its consequence.

citations.quote: However, if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.

claims.claim_text: The WAL cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction, so a very large write transaction can produce a very large WAL file until the transaction commits.

citations.quote: A checkpoint can only complete when no other transactions are running, which means the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction. So a large change to a large database might result in a large WAL file.
